item.title: APMT takes 49% stake in Haiphong’s HHIT terminal in northern Vietnam | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The move comes just days after a joint venture between the two companies was selected as the preferred bidder to develop a $1.8 billion container terminal in Da Nang.

item.title: FedEx Freight battles weak US industrial sector ahead of spinoff | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The latest quarterly results show that FedEx’s less-than-truckload division is struggling with lackluster industrial demand, but a change in strategy after a planned June spinoff could provide different results.

item.title: US resin shippers look to tap new customers amid Iran war | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has cut off a major source of global resin supply, teeing up US production to fill in some of the gap.

item.title: New shipping crisis brings ‘resilience’ question to the fore again | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the latest disruption to global shipping, highlighting once again that the market would rather ride out the problem than pay for the resilience that could bring relief, analyst Lars Jensen writes.

item.title: Houston cuts free time on reefer importers amid ongoing high dwells | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Reefer shipments into the port, while still small, have been growing faster than overall cargo, forcing port officials to deal with more long-dwelling containers.

item.title: FMC rejects requests by carriers to waive waiting period for Middle East surcharges | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The decision means CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd, Maersk and Zim will be forced to wait until early April before implementing surcharges designed to recoup higher operating costs associated with the war in the Middle East.

item.title: ONE takes stake in Busan’s Dongwon terminal ahead of Premier network shift | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The carrier alliance will shake up its Asia-Europe network in April with Busan becoming the focus of its North Asia trade and direct calls ending to ports in Japan and Taiwan.

item.title: US Gulf breakbulk ports lean into project boom | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Houston and New Orleans are coming off a year of growth for project cargo volumes, albeit with a drop in steel imports, and both ports anticipate a continuation of those trends.

item.title: UP adjusts intermodal pricing to win back volume as truckload rates climb | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Union Pacific for the second time in five weeks is resetting freight-all-kinds rates on key lanes for rail-owned boxes used by intermodal marketing companies.

item.title: War hands railroads the ‘gift’ of higher diesel prices | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The Iran-driven fuel spike has created the widest intermodal cost advantage in years, but capturing it — and keeping it — requires something railroads have rarely practiced: orchestrated intermodal, writes Paul Tonsager.
